CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female who underwent bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020. She reports that her breasts are doing well. She denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. She reports no longer experiencing back pain. Patient notes that during a visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was found under her left breast, but she has not felt it since then after performing massages. She reports that scars have been bothering her, particularly in one area, and she has been using scar gel daily. She states the gel has helped and she does not think she needs it as much now. Physical examination reveals bilateral breast incisions that are well healed with no signs of infection or redness. Some scar widening is noted, particularly in one area with high tension. Patient declines revision surgery at this time and agrees to follow up in six months to reassess.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting.

Bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed 10-10-2020.

ALLERGIES

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying summertime. Family is doing well.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breasts examined. Incisions well healed with no signs of infection or redness. Mild scar widening noted bilaterally, more prominent in one area with high tension. No hard spots, lumps, or bumps palpated.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Stable post-operative status following bilateral reduction mammoplasty with good healing. Continue mederma scar gel application twice daily with massage to bilateral scars. Follow up in six months to reassess scars and determine if revision surgery is desired. Patient to have photos taken today for documentation.
